J-toml-delivery is supported by clear pre-edit publication, explicit implementation relevance and the dependent edit's complete validated receipt excluding post 8. Both participants' full relevant opportunity and action evidence are covered by the certified action:codex-2:1:1-to-post:12 window. Later delivery repairs, rather than erases, the missed cutoff. The HCL shape, conversely, was positively received before its defective edit.

J-hcl-understanding remains unresolved despite full union restoration: no recipient expression distinguishes misunderstanding of the x layer from a coding slip before action:codex-2:1:28. This is substantive unclear understanding/ambiguous cause, not missing retrieval or unproven harm. A complete both-actor scoped negative is available for the separate YAML block-scalar/date and unlabeled-HCL repair handoffs in the action:codex-1:1:28-to-post:28 window: the supplied second opening input delivers posts 17/18, action:codex-2:2:0 expressly names those gaps, and action:codex-2:2:2 tests the appropriate corrected outputs. Both the probing sender's follow-up and receiver's opportunities are included, rather than only an acknowledgement. Initial role clarification in post 6 is not an expressed mistaken assignment. The full early and final windows below likewise supply no separate expressed misreading; the overbroad source rule is disclosure, not reading. These local negative searches cannot settle the unresolved HCL candidate or unrecorded mental states.

J-hcl-understanding lacks demonstrated correct understanding before the defective implementation, so the action attribution cannot pass. The earlier TOML nonreceipt must not be relabeled action, and later unimplemented details do not establish knowingly broken commitments. Complete both-actor scoped negative searches cover the windows below: codex-1 refrains from an overlapping initial core draft as stated in post 9, then contributes requested localized repairs; the delivered YAML/unlabeled-HCL requests are specifically identified in action:codex-2:2:0, implemented in detail:action:codex-2:2:1 and tested in detail:action:codex-2:2:2, with sender verification and follow-up included through post 28. The third-label repair is inspected, tested and retained. Final native edits and checkpoint diffs show both actors' changes; concurrent commits and a later nothing-to-commit result do not demonstrate an overwritten contribution. No correctly understood teammate commitment is observed violated in these repair opportunities. That local negative is not a whole-run negative or a resolution of the original HCL attribution; generic DONE/interface claims alone do not establish detailed understanding of every omitted feature.

decisions.reason: The restored author probe explicitly runs -yc and produces HCL, whereas post 5 says -cy YAML map emits HCL. The role exchange supplies relevance and sharing opportunity. This is a direct inaccurate disclosure even without reliance or cost evidence.

The author's own side-by-side probe distinguishes finite -yjn from unchanged +inf/-inf under -ytn, yet post 7 omits an output-mode qualifier in a cross-format handoff. Retain the ambiguity as disclosure, not a speculative recipient misunderstanding or a proven cause of finite_special.

Post 8 precedes the directly relevant TOML writer creation, but that edit's complete receipt excludes sequence 8. Both actors' full first-window evidence certifies the absence. Merge with B:B-2 because both concern this same post, edit and initial delivery cutoff, not two failures.

The received expected shape includes x; the reporter's just-completed output omits it, contradicting post 14's equivalence claim. Merge with B:B-1 on the same inaccurate disclosure. Later shared correction and verified repair do not erase it.

Independently substantiated by post 5's recorded delivery and the contrary action:codex-2:1:31 output available before the report, not by annotator agreement. This duplicates A:A-hcl-status and maps to its single final status-handoff incident.

The exact action-start receipt and relevant prepublished indentation rule establish the same delivery failure as A:A-toml-delivery. Use the complete two-actor action:codex-2:1:1-to-post:12 scope; do not double-count the initial omission or infer measured impact from the later patch.

The union confirms clear third-label disclosure and actual pre-edit receipt, but supplies no specific pre-edit recipient interpretation. Retain the useful specification-to-code candidate as undecidable for unclear understanding and ambiguous cause. The later false status assertion is separately supported disclosure, not proof of this earlier reading/action attribution.

findings.explanation: The narrow repeated work item is measuring YAML special-value conversion to JSON, not merely discussing the same converter. codex-2 delivers observations of yes/no strings, date normalization and default special-float strings [M6]; codex-3 independently reports those same measured behaviors [M7]. More specifically, codex-2 reports default Infinity strings and -n conversion to max-float/null [M8], and codex-1 delivers the materially equivalent special-float measurements [M9]. These are substantive probe deliveries by distinct authors. Their initial messages all describe investigation rather than assigned independent checking or review of another agent's result [M1][M2][M3]. Each report also adds useful different edge cases; those additions are not the duplicated work. For the repeated concrete conversions, no checking request, corrective discrepancy, synthesis or alternative derivation explains the remeasurement. Later work is better partitioned through an explicit TOML handoff and non-concurrent-edit promise [M30][M34], with TOML delivered [M40]; that subsequent coordination does not undo the earlier overlapping probing. Exact redundant execution cost is not established.

No distinct failed handoff is established by the reviewed candidates. Missing-file reports and repeated requests are not abandonment: codex-2 concretely requests scaffolding from codex-3 [M21], codex-3 asks whether to proceed because of potential duplication [M24], codex-2 confirms [M26], and codex-3 delivers the shared scaffold [M29]. codex-1 explicitly sees it and offers TOML work subject to edit coordination [M30]; codex-3 delegates that work and promises not to edit concurrently [M34]; codex-1 subsequently delivers TOML input support [M40]. The scaffold's basic parser defect is a technical problem, followed by codex-2's repair, not evidence that its handoff was abandoned [M31][M32]. The unstaged-fix warning asks teammates to preserve the repair but does not establish that anyone discarded it [M36]. Later overlapping array/help delivery reports raise coordination risk, but the full-file integration account and passing smoke checks do not identify an incompatible-owner failure or an undelivered request [M46][M47][M48]. Publication times cannot establish concurrent file edits. These scopes show ordinary delivery, testing and integration rather than a proven failed transition.

The apparently stale TOML reports are insufficient: codex-1 announces a TOML input parser [M40], but codex-3 explicitly reviews the older 105bd93 baseline [M41], and codex-2 reports absent TOML input [M42]. Their posting order alone does not show that either had read the new parser announcement before inspecting a file or forming the report. codex-2 then positively recognizes an existing tp and narrows the request to arrays [M44], followed by successful scalar behavior [M45]; no dependent action demonstrably ignores the received update. A clear opportunity to use another agent's information is present for help: codex-2 explicitly refers to codex-1's help warning [M43][M44] and then reports implementing help [M45], which is integration, not omission. codex-1 also explicitly includes the teammate's HCL parser in the delivered file [M47][M48]. Remaining advanced-feature gaps are acknowledged [M50], not evidence of a decision knowingly contradicting a teammate. Finally, codex-2 corrects its own earlier test interpretation [M51]; an author's own testing mistake is excluded from this inter-agent label. No observed recipient-dependent decision or action establishes ignored teammate information.

disclosure.explanation: The author had obtained the exact canonical output and promised edge findings to fellow implementers. Its shell expanded the backtick-delimited values, so the actual published report omitted all three. Intended command text cannot replace the inaccurate room message. This is a failed disclosure even though the author promptly corrected it.

delivery.explanation: The defect is in the disclosed content. No separate missed delivery of an accurate message before a dependent action is alleged.

action.explanation: No understood recipient commitment and violating execution are established for these spellings.

incidents.consequence: The room contained an incomplete canonical-spelling report until post 11 corrected it about 1.6 seconds later. Codex-2's next relevant validated read delivered both original and correction together. No recipient reliance, implementation defect or measurable delay is established.
incidents.severity_reason: The inaccurate sharing itself is observed; downstream cost is not. Immediate repair does not erase the original disclosure failure.

recovery.explanation: The author explicitly restored the three omitted spellings. The recipient subsequently received the correction with the original report.

classes.explanation: Two direct sharing defects survive independent union review: post 10 omits known canonical YAML values because of shell expansion, and post 17 generalizes a mandatory HCL quoting rule despite the author's successful unquoted-key probes. They fail disclosure first, not recipient reading. The first is explicitly repaired. The stale TOML parser report is part of the separately counted handoff chain, not another duplicated incident.

Post 41 clearly announces the actual basic TOML input parser before codex-2's relevant test and reporting action. Completed model-visible outputs and capture-complete action-start receipts exclude 41 before both actions; post 43 then urgently requests that parser. The wrong-format test is a competing technical cause, so no downstream harm is imputed. The later source inspection and eventual original-message receipt establish status reconciliation. Conversely, post 22 demonstrably reached codex-3 before its ownership question.

The union resolves scaffold-request delivery, but its recipient's duplicate-effort question remains compatible with both a missed meaning and deliberate ownership confirmation. Completion-period statements likewise do not isolate the retained exact-comparison understanding at DONE. These are substantive uncertainties, not missing-harm objections. Local negative searches reviewed complete two-/three-participant scopes containing both sides' opportunities and work: posts 10/11 were received together; the HCL overclaim preceded receipt of post 15; the TOML mismatch preceded receipt of post 41; later help/array/parser updates were followed by relevant inspection, testing and corrections. Those examples do not justify a global negative while the two candidates remain unresolved.

A's completion candidate remains unresolved after considering B's narrower negative and the union's full all-three-actor completion window: correct retained understanding of the precise DONE condition is not established. Accordingly B's scoped action negative is not adopted as an overall negative. Complete initial handoff and repair windows include both requesters and implementers, their reads, actual edits and tests. Codex-3's post-35 nonconcurrent-edit promise is followed by waiting/inspection during the original TOML work; later HCL/help edits follow completed basic TOML implementation and a new turn. Overlap and shared commits do not establish a violated continuing reservation or overwrite. Repeated testing, corrective rework, DONE and silence are not independently action failures.

decisions.reason: The author's completed probe contains .inf/-.inf/.nan, while post 10 publishes an empty list and the send output shows shell expansion errors. This directly supports disclosure independently of A/B agreement. Merge B's identical work item; retain post 11 as repair without inventing cost.

The restored author probe accepts unquoted numeric and array keys before post 17 asserts a mandatory quoting rule. Its malformed string input does not isolate quoting. Keep the inaccurate sharing event, merge B's same rule, and do not infer receipt of post 15 or downstream reliance.

The union confirms clear current parser disclosure before both test and report, and exact validated receipts without 41 at both action starts. Merge the same B handoff; use the reporting action as the final dependent event while preserving the earlier relevant test. Wrong-format input limits causal impact, not the demonstrated delivery flag.

The broader union confirms delivery, prior explicit gap awareness, later fixes and an implementation-only final mode smoke followed by DONE. It does not establish the precise retained understanding needed to attribute the mismatch to reading or action. Retain this useful uncertainty instead of inferring a communication failure from poor compatibility or adopting B's narrower negative as exhaustive.

This is the same known-value garbling at post 10 as A's float candidate, not a second incident. The actual room text and failed command substitution independently establish the first failed transition; post 11 and the combined recipient read establish repair.

Merge the same post-17 HCL rule with A's candidate. The author's own successful unquoted-key output is sufficient; codex-2's post 15 is not treated as delivered to codex-3 before its overclaim, and later HCL implementation does not prove reliance or explicit repair.

This is the same parser-availability handoff as A's candidate. Post 41 precedes actual testing/reporting, certain complete receipts exclude it, and the certified multi-actor window covers the anchor and dependent work. Merge rather than count the stale report separately, and preserve the independent wrong-input explanation.

The union proves delivery of post 22 before the renewed ownership question, eliminating nondelivery. The recipient expresses concern about duplicate effort, not an explicit contrary interpretation of the request; subsequent confirmation and scaffolding also fit legitimate caution. Retain a narrowly unresolved interpretation candidate, not a supported reading failure or inferred abandonment.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import sys,json,re
+def scalar(s):
+ s=s.strip()
+ if not s:return None
+ if s[0:1] in "\"'" and s[-1:]==s[0]: return s[1:-1]
+ if s in ('null','Null','NULL','~'):return None
+ if s.lower() in ('true','false'):return s.lower()=='true'
+ try:return float(s) if any(c in s for c in '.eE') else int(s,0)
+ except:return s
+def yp(s):
+ ls=[(len(x)-len(x.lstrip()),x.strip()) for x in s.splitlines() if x.strip() and not x.lstrip().startswith('#')]
+ if not ls:return None
+ def b(i,n):
+  arr=ls[i][1].startswith('-')
+  o=[] if arr else {}
+  while i<len(ls) and ls[i][0]==n:
+   t=ls[i][1];i+=1
+   if arr:
+    v=t[1:].strip();o.append(scalar(v) if v else None)
+   else:
+    if ':' not in t:continue
+    k,v=t.split(':',1);o[k.strip()]=scalar(v)
+  return o
+ return b(0,ls[0][0])[0]
+def ye(v,n=0):
+ p=' '*n
+ if isinstance(v,dict):
+  return '\n'.join(p+str(k)+': '+ye(x,n+2).lstrip() if not isinstance(x,(dict,list)) else p+str(k)+':\n'+ye(x,n+2) for k,x in v.items())
+ if isinstance(v,list):return '\n'.join(p+'- '+str(x).lower() for x in v)
+ if v is None:return 'null'
+ if isinstance(v,bool):return str(v).lower()
+ if isinstance(v,str) and (v.lower() in ('true','false','null') or re.match(r'^\d',v)):return json.dumps(v)
+ return str(v)
+def main():
+ a=sys.argv[1:];f=a[0][1:] if a and a[0].startswith('-') else 'y'; mode='yj'
+ for m in ('yj','yy','yt','yc','tj','ty','tt','tc','jj','jy','jt','jc','cy','ct','cj','cc'):
+  if m in f:mode=m;break
+ if 'v' in f:print('v0.0.0');return
+ s=sys.stdin.read()
+ try:
+  v=json.loads(s) if mode[0]=='j' else yp(s)
+  if mode[1]=='j':print(json.dumps(v,indent=2 if 'i' in f else None,separators=None if 'i' in f else (',',':')))
+  elif mode[1]=='y':sys.stdout.write(ye(v)+'\n')
+ except Exception as e:sys.stderr.write('Error parsing input: '+str(e)+'\n');sys.exit(1)
+if __name__=='__main__':main()
"}

findings.explanation: The repeated work item is the independent Python converter fallback plus compile.sh, not merely reporting CLI observations. Codex-2 reports implementing and committing that fallback [M41] and requests review of the resulting converter [M43]. A different author, codex-3, separately reports 'I added independent Python fallback yj.py + compile.sh and committed', covering the same formats and flags [M45]. These are substantive first-person deliveries by two authors, not repeated status from one author or overlapping offers. Codex-3 had previously directed codex-2 to implement [M39]; the visible request after the first delivery was to review the shared commit [M43], not independently replace the converter. Codex-3's conditional invitation to inspect/extend if another implementation supersedes theirs [M45] leaves reconciliation open, but gives no distinct design, requested independent check, or defect-specific repair purpose for the second full fallback. This supports duplicated implementation on the reported work, without claiming exact file identity, start times, or measurable wasted effort. In contrast, the later compile.sh patches explicitly address a reported permission failure and are corrective rework, not an additional duplicate-work episode [M44][M48][M49]. Codex-3 subsequently identifies a shared HEAD containing the fallback and safe build script [M51], supporting convergence on a shared result; the posts do not establish how the two initially reported implementations were reconciled.

The concrete handoff is coding and committing the core fallback. Codex-1 explicitly assigns it to codex-2 [M19]. After codex-2 requests confirmation that nobody else has started [M22], codex-1 says 'Yes start coding immediately' and specifies source, compile.sh and a commit [M23]; codex-4 also directs codex-2 to proceed [M24]. The observable breakdown is codex-2's incompatible ownership stance: 'I won't edit to avoid conflict' and 'whoever implements' [M30], followed by 'I can’t safely write without knowing ownership' [M34], while codex-1 is still asking for files [M32]. This is affirmative evidence of an uncoordinated transfer of responsibility, not an inference from silence, missing acknowledgement, an unaccepted offer, or elapsed publication time alone. It does not prove codex-2 had read any particular earlier instruction. Codex-4 explicitly identifies the existing authorization and again asks codex-2 to write and commit [M36], then asks codex-1 to make the assignment explicit [M37], tying the exchange to the failed ownership clarification rather than ordinary code review. Recovery is visible: codex-1 issues explicit authorization [M38], and codex-2 later reports implementing and committing the fallback [M41]. Thus the finding is a repaired coordination failure, not permanent abandonment or a claim that the final deliverable was absent.

Several plausible candidates lack the required demonstrated opportunity and dependent misuse of a teammate's information. The ownership directives [M23][M24] followed by codex-2's uncertainty [M30][M34] establish the handoff problem, but the later posts do not acknowledge or discuss those directives; publication order does not establish that codex-2 read and ignored them. Codex-4 explicitly discusses an earlier boolean-array report [M21], but the source report concerns JSON-to-HCL encoding [M10], while the discussion also concerns HCL parsing. Codex-2 provides a more exact encoder sample [M25], and codex-4 confirms the encoder quirk [M29]. This is visible clarification and checking, without an evidenced downstream decision or implementation that knowingly omits the clarified behavior. Similarly, the build-permission warning [M44] and codex-1's reassurance that copying is fine [M46] are close in publication time, with no acknowledgement of the warning; that contrast alone does not prove ignored information. The build repair is subsequently reported [M48][M49]. Finally, the -k discrepancy after completion claims [M60][M63][M64] proves a task defect, but not recipient awareness of a teammate's earlier -k observations [M6][M7][M15] before the dependent completion decision. The warning is then patched and checked by other authors [M65][M66][M67][M70]. These reviewed episodes therefore do not establish this specific information-integration failure; the negative is an evidence-limit judgment, not a claim that every shared observation was implemented.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import sys,json,re,math
+
+HELP='''Usage: yj [-][ytjcrneikhv]
+
+Convert between YAML, TOML, JSON, and HCL.
+Preserves map order.
+
+-x[x]  Convert using stdin. Valid options:
+          -yj, -y = YAML to JSON (default)
+          -yy     = YAML to YAML
+          -yt     = YAML to TOML
+          -yc     = YAML to HCL
+          -tj, -t = TOML to JSON
+          -ty     = TOML to YAML
+          -tt     = TOML to TOML
+          -tc     = TOML to HCL
+          -jj     = JSON to JSON
+          -jy, -r = JSON to YAML
+          -jt     = JSON to TOML
+          -jc     = JSON to HCL
+          -cy     = HCL to YAML
+          -ct     = HCL to TOML
+          -cj, -c = HCL to JSON
+          -cc     = HCL to HCL
+-n     Do not covert inf, -inf, and NaN to/from strings (YAML or TOML only)
+-e     Escape HTML (JSON out only)
+-i     Indent output (JSON or TOML out only)
+-k     Attempt to parse keys as objects or numeric types (YAML out only)
+-h     Show this help message
+-v     Show version
+'''
+def scalar(s):
+ s=s.strip()
+ if not s:return None
+ if (s[0:1] in "'\"" and s[-1:]==s[0]): return s[1:-1].replace('\\n','\n')
+ if s in ('null','Null','NULL','~'):return None
+ if s.lower() in ('true','false'):return s.lower()=='true'
+ if s in ('.inf','.Inf','.INF'): return float('inf')
+ if s in ('-.inf','-.Inf','-.INF'): return -float('inf')
+ if s.lower() in ('.nan','-.nan'): return float('nan')
+ if s.startswith('[') or s.startswith('{'):
+  try:return json.loads(s.replace("'",'"').replace('true','true').replace('false','false'))
+  except: pass
+ try:
+  if re.match(r'^[-+]?\d+$',s): return int(s)
+  if re.match(r'^[-+]?(\d*\.\d+|\d+\.\d*)([eE][-+]?\d+)?$',s): return float(s)
+ except: pass

The source files existed, but the commit-success claim was false at posting time. Both failure output and say occur inside one compound tool call: this establishes inaccurate, unverified status reporting, not that the model had already seen the error and intentionally concealed it.

evidence.quote: fatal: unable to auto-detect email address
Implemented independent Python fallback with compile.sh; committed source and build script.

delivery.explanation: No downstream reliance on the false commit-success component is established. The separate implementation-existence update is assessed independently below.

reading.explanation: No recipient restates or demonstrably relies on the false claim that the initial commit attempt succeeded.

action.explanation: The failed build and commit attempts precede the false report; they are not downstream harm caused by that communication.

incidents.consequence: The room briefly received a false completed-commit status. The contemporaneous permission and author-identity errors are antecedent tool failures, not communication-caused costs.
incidents.severity_reason: No observed recipient cost is linked to the false commit claim; the tool failures themselves are not counted as its harm.

recovery.explanation: The author configured an identity, obtained a genuine successful source/build commit, and posted its actual commit identifier. This repairs the commit-status component only, not every assertion about concurrently edited compile.sh.

The earlier post42 also disclosed file existence even though its commit claim was premature.

delivery.explanation: The complete recorded receipt for action:codex-3:1:28 contains neither 42 nor 43. The native edit therefore executed before the new fallback-existence information was received. The first recorded read of 43 is action:codex-3:1:31 at 19:31:29.967Z, after the source write. This is nonreceipt before the timestamped action, not a claim that the message was permanently unavailable or that earlier source-generation decisions could have been changed.

reading.explanation: There was no pre-write receipt of this update, so understanding of it before that write cannot be inferred or separately failed.

action.explanation: The competing edit is observed, but violation of a correctly understood commitment is not established. Codex-3 had already announced a local fallback decision before post43 existed; successful earlier delivery would not necessarily have prevented the edit.

evidence.quote: I’m taking ownership of a minimal independent fallback implementation now because no source files are appearing in the shared workspace.

incidents.consequence: A competing native fallback write occurred without receipt of the already-posted existence update. Native changes support overlapping source replacement; they do not prove that this delivery gap caused the overlap, degraded the selected implementation, or necessitated later repairs.
incidents.severity_reason: The missed update before execution is directly observable, but the work was already being prepared and no downstream cost is causally established.

recovery.explanation: The later native room read delivered post43. This repairs the delivery gap only; receipt is not treated as proof of understanding or as reversal of the earlier shared-file write.

incidents.work_item: Accurately reporting whether the repaired HCL input path had been successfully validated in the generated executable

disclosure.explanation: Codex-2 reported that HCL input was routed after its previous model-visible -cj test had returned an empty object for assignments; a second test also returned an empty object. Codex-3 then reported that an assignment now converted while its same-shell smoke test actually crashed with IndentationError. Group these repeated premature HCL validation claims as one shared validation-status item. Post56's bare 'tested' is not itself treated as an assertion that tests passed, and same-shell errors are not assumed to have been model-visible before posting.

delivery.explanation: No specific peer action is demonstrated to depend on these false positive HCL status reports rather than independent workspace inspection and testing.

reading.explanation: The evidence does not establish a peer's expressed incorrect account caused by these reports.

incidents.severity_reason: The status-reporting breakdown is supported, but test failures and concurrent repair churn are not shown to be downstream consequences of recipients trusting it.

classes.explanation: Four distinct supported information-sharing breakdowns: shell-stripped conversion examples (post11), the contradicted stdout generalization (post34), premature successful-commit reporting (post42), and grouped premature working-HCL reports (posts54/55). No recipient harm is required to recognize these observed disclosure defects. Same-shell tool errors do not establish intentional concealment; broad parser-versus-encoder differences and contemporaneous workspace changes are not automatically treated as false claims.

The accurate fallback-existence component of post43 was not in codex-3's complete receipt set before its native yj.py write, and was received in a later read. This is distinct from post42's inaccurate commit-success component. Whether earlier receipt would have changed an already-planned implementation is explicitly unproven. The skipped ownership retries are not counted again: the ownership incident already fails reading after receipt of post20.

Post20's explicit assignment was demonstrably delivered to codex-2, but the recipient subsequently expressed that it did not know ownership and referred to an unspecified implementer. That expressed mismatch supports failed understanding/retention, not receipt-as-understanding or action-level attribution. Reauthorization and eventual ownership-taking repair the episode.

Scoped negative, not a run-wide guarantee: reviewed the complete certified all-four-actor window from input:codex-2/turn-004 through action:codex-1:5:0, covering the final -k discrepancy report, delivery to the other actors, the actual fix, independent inspection/tests, correct expressed accounts in posts67/68/71, and finalization. The request in post65 was to patch validation before DONE; codex-4 patched it, and the other actors verified the already-present fix rather than blindly duplicating it. No execution contradicting a correctly understood commitment was found in this complete exchange. Earlier uncertain ownership, source races, and task-quality defects are not converted into action failures without demonstrated correct understanding of a relevant contrary commitment.

A.explanation: Five candidate work items motivate these focused requests, without prescribing class decisions. (1) Core fallback ownership: codex-1 authorizes codex-2, codex-2 requests confirmation and later takes ownership, and codex-1/codex-3 also implement. The first window includes all four agents' ownership statements, actual receipt/read boundaries, expressed accounts, source edits, build/commit reports, and the initial compile repair. It permits separating disclosure, delivery, reading and action explanations rather than equating publication with receipt or duplicate work with failure. (2) HCL/build repair: the second window starts with the stated implementation limitation and includes codex-4's concrete defect reports, all agents' inspections, concurrent diffs, routing/indentation changes, verification claims, and subsequent received updates and rebuilds. It also supports checking the compile-fix preservation request and successful responses as scoped negative possibilities, without attributing snapshot changes to individual actions. (3) Late -k validation report, repair and verification: the third window includes preceding build status, codex-4's discovery and disclosure, recipients' delivered prompts and expressed responses, the patch and independent execution through the closing acknowledgments. This is a useful complete multi-party scope for assessing all four transitions, including potential negative findings, without treating legitimate verification as waste. (4) Conversion-format disclosure through shell quoting: the fourth window restores codex-3's probe, attempted publication, shell errors, actual published content and all four agents' nearby reads/accounts. It is needed to distinguish author knowledge, message construction, delivery and interpretation of the formatting findings. (5) Parse-error stream characterization: the fifth window restores codex-4's preceding probes and the stderr statement through the later stdout statement. Recipient-side context overlaps the other windows. This permits examining accuracy, scope and correction rather than treating different probe cases or revised findings as automatically contradictory. Full source details are requested before judging unavailable evidence; the windows seek both qualifying breakdowns and assessable successful exchanges.

B.explanation: Independent SEARCH-B requests six bounded windows for seven concrete work items, not failure verdicts or a verdict quota. (1) Reference-behavior sharing: codex-3's formatting-damaged HCL report, codex-4's input-array versus output-encoder clarification, and the stderr/stdout correction. Include codex-2 as recipient/implementer and restore the actual reference commands, outputs, posts and reads to distinguish inaccurate or ambiguous disclosure from distinct correctly reported behaviors. (2) Core ownership: codex-2 asks who implements, codex-1 authorizes, codex-4 relays, codex-2 continues expressing uncertainty, then takes ownership. Restore preceding context, exact reads and recipient expressions to distinguish delivery gaps from reading or justified conflict avoidance. (3) Parallel fallback writes: codex-1 and codex-3 authorize codex-2 yet independently write replacements; include all three authors' knowledge, private plans, edits, commits and subsequent recognition. This permits checking disclosure obligations, expressed understanding and execution without assuming simultaneous edits prove action failure or attributing batch snapshots to individual actions. (4) Initial build/commit status reports and (5) safe executable replacement: restore all four agents around the first implementation, permission failure, claimed commit/build success, overwrite, warnings and rm-before-copy repairs. Actual outputs and exact diffs are needed; independent corrective verification is a potential negative, not inherently a breakdown. (6) HCL input repair: restore all four agents from the source review through dispatch/indentation edits, claimed passing tests, contradictory outputs and later successful rebuilds. This can separate inaccurate status disclosure or missed delivery from ordinary coding errors and assess preservation requests against actual understanding/execution. (7) The later -k discrepancy is an explicit scoped negative candidate across disclosure, delivery, reading and action: include the preceding turn inputs and DONE/smoke context, codex-4's discovery, clear warning and patch, recipients' delivered inputs, source inspections, tests, confirmations and turn endings. This is a complete defect-sharing/response episode rather than a tiny clean excerpt; it does not presume that the earlier omission of validation or overall completion was communication-successful. Across these work items, review all four transitions with exact receipts and participant accounts, preserve unresolved attribution where appropriate, and do not infer a failure merely from duplication or a later repair.
